anti_overlap: fd-llm-pipeline-cost focuses on subprocess count per run
fd-cache-dynamics focuses on prompt caching within a run
fd-synthesis-batching focuses on merging calls within a run
decision_lens: Findings ranked by cost-avoidance impact per re-run. A book with good existing artifacts should re-run only synthesis, not the full pipeline.
focus: Artifact caching and conditional execution: which pipeline phases can be skipped based on existing artifacts
name: fd-skip-and-cache-strategy
persona: A pipeline reliability engineer who focuses on idempotency and incremental execution. Understands --reuse-source-run skips chunk extraction, and wants to know whether other phases are also skipped correctly.
review_areas: Verify --reuse-source-run skips outline and keyword extraction in addition to chunk extraction
Check whether chunk_cache_base hash invalidates correctly when extraction prompt changes but source text doesn't
Identify whether there's a skip mechanism for self-check when synthesis results are reused unchanged
Assess whether --score-only correctly bypasses all 17 non-QS framework calls
Flag proposals for parallel book-level runs and verify artifact path prevents cross-book cache collisions
Check whether failed synthesis calls are persisted to disk, enabling partial re-runs
success_hints: A --skip-synthesis-check flag would save 1 call per re-score run
Per-framework artifact persistence would enable targeted re-runs of failed frameworks
task_context: The NTSMR pipeline uses claude -p as a subprocess backend. Each invocation carries ~$0.18 overhead from a 66K system prompt. Pipeline: outline (1) → keywords (1) → chunk extractions (N) → 18 framework syntheses → self-check (1), plus repair retries.
